title: Brucie Ramon: The Reluctant Recruit Turned Final Boss
body: Ramon wasn't even sure he wanted to join the Buckaroo Football League, and for a while his Araleasers played like it. The 2023 debut went 4-10 on 1,375.3 points, earned the 6 seed and finished fifth of six, saved from the basement only by Sonny's Ben Dover. Two pickups all season and zero trades. Brucie was set-it-and-forget-it before set-it-and-forget-it got him into trouble.

Then 2024 happened, and the guy who didn't want to be here nearly won the whole thing. A 7-7 record and 1,430.9 points earned the 3 seed, Ramon won his semifinal (still his only playoff win), and the Araleasers marched into Buckaroo Bowl II. Waiting there was Kaushal's Habibsters, who finished the job and took their second straight title. Habib has been Brucie's nightmare all along: 4-8 head to head, plus Ramon's career-worst 56.4 in week 12 that year. All of that came with exactly one waiver pickup, the least effort any manager has ever put into a runner-up finish.

2025 is the chapter that will hang in the league museum forever. The Araleasers went 5-11 on a career-high 1,523.7 points, finished fifth of six, and somewhere in there the ledger shows four trades and eight pickups. But the real headline came after week 8, when Ramon was removed for inactivity. The team was renamed Ramon's Remains, beat Alan in its very first game without him and kept piling up wins, all counted on Brucie's record with an asterisk. Few managers have been outcoached by their own absence.

Which brings us to 2026 and No Banner only HULK, the most infuriating team in the league because it's Brucie's. It opened with a 177.9-point demolition of Mekhi, the best week of Ramon's career, and is now 6-1 with 927.4 points and a 37 percent shot at the title. One trade and four pickups say he's actually showing up this time. Kai would like a word: Ramon owns him 6-3, the most lopsided rivalry on his sheet, and he's a perfect 1-0 against both rookies on the block, Zoe and Jordan.

So here stands the Bills-loving Chicago turncoat, everybody's favorite guy to root against, holding the hottest hand in the league. His career head-to-heads are still underwater against Sonny (5-7), Randy (4-7) and Alan (5-6), and his trophy case is empty. If the rest of the league wants to stop him, the scouting report is simple: get under his skin, because nothing on the field has slowed him down yet.
